title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback
authors: Long Ouyang, Jeff Wu, Xu Jiang, Diogo Almeida, Carroll L. Wainwright, Pamela Mishkin, Chong Zhang, Sandhini Agarwal, Katarina Slama, Alex Ray, John Schulman, Jacob Hilton, Fraser Kelton, Luke Miller, Maddie Simens, Amanda Askell, Peter Welinder, Paul Christiano, Jan Leike, Ryan Lowe
lab: OpenAI (a joint project of the Alignment team; Ryan Lowe and Jan Leike team leads)
date: March 2022 (arXiv v1, 4 March 2022, the only version)

code.title: following-instructions-human-feedback
code.note: no training code or weights: the model card, samples from GPT-3 and InstructGPT on the public NLP benchmarks, and links to the labeling instructions (about 10 minutes to skim)
code.label: samples, no code

paper_note: a long paper: 20 pages of main text, then references and 43 pages of appendices
takeaway: Defined the 3-stage RLHF recipe (SFT -> reward model -> PPO with KL penalty, plus PPO-ptx to cut the alignment tax) that made a 1.3B model preferred over 175B GPT-3 and became the ChatGPT-era industry standard.
verdict: Believe the recipe and the ordering it produced (PPO above SFT above prompted GPT-3 above GPT-3, with tight intervals, held-out labelers agreeing, and the head-to-head numbers consistent with Figure 1). Read the 1.3B-over-175B headline as true for this prompt distribution judged by these 40 labelers, and the truthfulness and toxicity gains as smaller than the text states: about 1.4 to 1.5 times on TruthfulQA by human labels, not twice, and 16 to 20% less toxicity, not 25%.

headline.k: 1.3B InstructGPT and 175B GPT-3, each against 175B SFT
headline.d: the smallest InstructGPT beats GPT-3 with 135 times its parameters

headline.k: 175B InstructGPT preferred to 175B GPT-3, head to head
headline.d: 71 ± 4% against GPT-3 given a well-chosen few-shot prompt

headline.k: to train 175B PPO-ptx, against 3,640 to pretrain GPT-3

resources.t: Aligning language models to follow instructions
resources.by: OpenAI blog, 27 January 2022 (before the arXiv version)
resources.n: the announcement: InstructGPT replaced GPT-3 as the default API model, with side-by-side samples.

resources.t: RLHF: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
resources.n: the whole pipeline (pretrain, SFT, reward model, PPO) with the maths, the data economics and practical failure modes; the best single walkthrough of what this paper standardised.

resources.t: Illustrating Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF)
resources.by: Lambert, Castricato, von Werra, Havrilla (Hugging Face)
resources.n: the canonical diagram-first explanation of the three stages and the KL-penalised reward.
book-length treatment of RLHF and post-training; the reward-modelling and policy-optimisation chapters (about 2 hours) put InstructGPT in the context of everything after it (DPO, GRPO, RLVR).

resources.t: The N+ Implementation Details of RLHF with PPO
resources.by: Huang, Noukhovitch, Hosseini, Rasul, Wang, Tunstall (arXiv 2403.17031)
resources.n: the first open reproduction of OpenAI's RLHF scaling results, with over 20 implementation details that decide whether PPO on a language model works at all; read it before implementing the recipe.

resources.t: Scaling Laws for Reward Model Overoptimization
resources.n: the measurement this paper's KL penalty guards against: a gold reward model stands in for humans, and the true score rises and then falls as a proxy reward model is optimised harder.

kb.n: 2020: the base models and the architecture; InstructGPT is GPT-3 plus human-feedback fine-tuning.
2022: replaces the human harmlessness labels with AI feedback (RLAIF) on the same RLHF skeleton.
2023: collapses the reward model and PPO stages into one classification loss on the same comparisons.
2024: GRPO drops the value function this paper initialised from the reward model and moves the KL term into the loss.
2025: rule-based (verifiable) rewards instead of a learned reward model for reasoning data.
2024: an open production pipeline built on the SFT plus preference-tuning template.
2025: a fully open pipeline (the Tülu 3 recipe: SFT, DPO, RLVR).

kb.t: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
kb.n: 2020: the scaling this paper argues post-training beats, for usefulness, by 100 times.

topics.n: where SFT, preference tuning and RL sit in today's post-training pipelines.
PPO, KL-regularised policy optimisation and the methods that replaced it.
